horses.spotlight_comment: This looks a good opportunity for C&D winner UN SENS A LA VIE who was a respectable fourth in gruelling conditions in a major handicap at Newbury in February. He sets a useful standard back in much calmer waters and should be hard to beat in his bid to make it 3-6 over hurdles. The main threat could come from dual course winner Snatch A Glance who was disputing the lead when he fell three out in a novice here on his reappearance last month.[David Moon] Page 1 spotlightludlow 22.04.26

Several have possibilities but the most striking contender is MAXIMUM OFFERS who was a runaway winner over fences at Hereford last week. He's a major player again off 5lb higher back over hurdles and his yard won this race last year. Tzarmix has been knocking on the door since his C&D win in December and he's feared most, ahead of Noonetellsmenothin and The Egyptian Ginge. Another to keep an eye on is handicap newcomer Catwalk Girl.[David Moon] Page 2 spotlightludlow 22.04.26

Slevin 5-1 115 112 123 Three wins at around 2m in Ireland and latest was over fences for Willie Mullins in June 2023; record of 0-8 for current yard but he rallied well when a creditable third here (2m, good) last month; this is a different test at this new trip but he's well treated on his old form and needs watching in the market; tongue-tie back on. Gris Majeur 9 11-7 Sheila Lewis Sean Houlihan 9-2 113 113 125 Triple hurdle winner who made the breakthrough over fences in a Ludlow handicap (2m4f, good to firm) in October; that was a four-runner race but he's been placed in four runs since including when runner-up at Chepstow (2m7f) 11 days ago; should go well again and all of his wins have been on good/good to firm. Arrycan 12 11-5 N Scholfield Jack Quinlan 10-1 111 70 120 12yo who has won four times over fences but there were more bad runs than good ones in Ireland last year; on workable mark in suitable conditions but he was tailed off when last seen in October and needs a major revival for new yard. Petty Cash 9 11-2t1 H Daly Sam Twiston-Davies 9-1 108 108 127 Won over fences at Chepstow (2m7f, good to soft) in November 2024 but he's not seen much action since; ran well after wind surgery when third over C&D in February but he was pulled up at Newbury (2m6f) last month; tongue-tie is now added and he needs to bounce back again after that last run. Annie Express 8 11-0v R Llewellyn Toby McCain-Mitchell (5) 2-1 106 96 127 Has a patchy profile but she made it 2-6 over fences when justifying favouritism here (2m4f, good) last month; up 6lb but that was a personal best last time and her other chase win came over this C&D; key player. Zacony Rebel 11 10-2tb S Davies Charlie Price 40-1 94 105 123 Won a five-runner handicap at Huntingdon (2m7f, soft) in December but this veteran has struggled in five subsequent runs; has lots to prove and he's a long way out of the weights.

Preference is for C&D winner ANNIE EXPRESS (nap) who made it 2-6 over fences when justifying favouritism over 2m4f here last month. She remains feasibly treated off her revised mark and is open to more progress on this step back up in trip. The main threat could come from the in-form 9yo Gris Majeur who was runner-up in a similar race at Chepstow 11 days ago. Another to consider is last year's winner Almazhar Garde who could be a handful if he can get back on track.[David Moon] Page 3 spotlightludlow 22.04.26

The resurgent veteran Imperial Pride has had a win and a second over fences in her last two starts and is a big player if she can continue the good work back over hurdles. Klervia has claims if she can build on her promising fourth at Exeter, while Shes All Pride enters the reckoning after her creditable effort from out of the weights at Stratford. However, the vote goes to AFTER MANY DAYS who has finished runner-up in her last three handicaps and remains feasibly treated on her best form.[David Moon] Page 4 spotlightludlow 22.04.26

Preference is for MILLY OCEAN who showed clear promise with her debut fourth at Huntingdon last month and represents a yard with a record of 2-3 in bumpers here this season. Mysti Meadow and Britway Belle could be the pick of the other runners with experience, although there are several newcomers who need a close look including Meliden Mountain and Thatsnotmyname.[David Moon] Page 6 spotlightludlow 22.04.26

This looks tricky but it might be worth siding with PROHUS YANK who has had only two runs over regulation fences and ties in with subsequent Cheltenham and Aintree hero Barton Snow on a piece of C&D form in February. Potters Party looks the main danger, although Mr Glass was useful in his prime and could make a serious impact if he can build on his third at Exeter last month.[David Moon] Page 7
